subject: Medforge Community Makerspace Development
overview: John Petrella interviewed Trey Winter about the launch of the Medforge Community Makerspace, a non-profit providing residents with access to industrial tools and technical training. The discussion covered the organization’s search for a permanent facility, current home maintenance classes, and upcoming community fundraising events.

items.title: Introduction and Personal Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced guest Trey Winter, who discussed his background in astrophysics and his transition to becoming a resident and maker in Medford.

items.title: Origins of Medforge
items.summary: Winter described the inspiration for the makerspace as a response to the loss of local workshops during the pandemic and a desire to foster a local creative community.

items.title: Facility Search and City Partnerships
items.summary: Winter explained that Medforge is currently in a pre-launch phase while seeking a 10,000 square foot industrial space and awaiting news on a $1.3 million grant application submitted in partnership with the city.

items.title: Economic and Community Impact
items.summary: The discussion highlighted how makerspaces support the local economy by keeping leisure spending within the city and providing trade-skill training for adults.

items.title: Intro to Household Tools Classes
items.summary: Winter detailed a series of hands-on classes funded by a Medford City Community Fund grant that teach residents basic carpentry and home repair skills.

items.title: Welcome to Deadford Halloween Fundraiser
items.summary: Winter promoted the organization's 'Welcome to Deadford' Halloween ball scheduled for October 31, which features 3D-printed decor and local vendor partnerships.

items.title: Future Programming and Membership Model
items.summary: Winter announced upcoming participation in Medford Open Studios on November 14 and discussed plans for a tiered membership model that includes volunteer-based access.
